Retrieves the production bonus information for a specific company. Re-verified live after the v0.27 update (2026-10-26, companies-get-employees patch): the response shrank a lot — strategicBonus, ethicSpecializationBonus and ethicDepositBonus are gone (party ethics and strategic-resource production bonuses were both removed this patch), leaving only depositBonus and total. depositBonus is now always 0 on every company we checked, since this same patch also turned off deposits entirely (country specialization removed) — the field still exists but there's currently no way for it to be non-zero. There is no separate region-level production-bonus endpoint; a company's own +5% core-region bonus (new in v0.27) is applied server-side and isn't broken out anywhere in this response.

post.description: Retrieves one item's trading document. values holds the last 30 days, oldest first, with the last row being the current (in-progress) day — confirmed live: avgValue always equals totalValue / totalQuantity on every row, and currentValue equals the last row's avgValue. sellOrders/buyOrders came back empty on every item checked, so they're typed unknown[] here rather than guessed at. An item with no trading record at all (e.g. a toolbox) answers 404 NOT_FOUND, not an empty document.

Retrieves the paginated manager job market — companies currently looking for a manager (v0.27's new 'Managers' feature, added alongside hired employees: a manager is a player hired to run another player's company for a cut of its production). Confirmed live and reachable with our normal keys. Params are a guess by analogy with this spec's other getManyPaginated endpoints (limit/cursor) — not confirmed against a real zod error, since this procedure doesn't reject unknown or missing fields. Checked live 2026-11-09 over 1000 offers: `minManagement` is on about half of them, the older `citizenship` (country id) on about 8%, and an optional free-text `text` on a few — all optional, so an offer can carry either one or neither. (An earlier note that citizenship was replaced by minManagement was wrong.) limit is at most 50.

post.description: Retrieves every employee the calling account owns, across all of its companies (v0.27's new hired-employee system). Confirmed live and reachable with our normal, non-premium keys — scoped to whichever account the API key itself belongs to, no parameters taken. Each employee carries its stats (base/trained/revealed), traits, potential, wage, wageExpectation, training/specialization history, happiness breakdown, production bonus breakdown, and an `estimate` of its own hourly output: `production` is raw production POINTS per hour, not money (multiply by gameStat.getPpMoneyValue to get money), and `wage` is money per hour. These sum exactly to the company-level `hourly` totals from employee.getCompanyRoster. Reads the calling account's own data: with our API keys (accounts without employees) it returns an empty result, so the stored example is from an earlier account with employees.

Retrieves a one-call summary of the calling account's entire workforce across all companies: headcount, how many are trainable today, how many managers are assigned, toolboxes found so far, and hourly totals: `production` in raw production POINTS (multiply by gameStat.getPpMoneyValue to get money), toolbox find rate, and `wageCost` and `managerCost` in money. Confirmed live and reachable with our normal, non-premium keys; no parameters taken. Reads the calling account's own data: with our API keys (accounts without employees) it returns an empty result, so the stored example is from an earlier account with employees.

Retrieves one company's employee roster — same per-employee shape as employee.getMyEmployees. Confirmed live, public and reachable with our normal, non-premium keys for ANY companyId, not just ones the calling key's account owns.

Like employee.getCompanyEmployees, but also includes an `hourly` block with the company-wide totals — confirmed these are the exact sum, across every employee, of each one's own `estimate.production`/`estimate.wage`: `{production, toolboxes, wageCost, managerCost, cap}`. `production` is raw production POINTS per hour, NOT money, while `wageCost` and `managerCost` are money per hour, so production has to be converted before subtracting. This is the single best source for a company's current real employee profit: hourly profit = hourly.production * gameStat.getPpMoneyValue - hourly.wageCost - hourly.managerCost, live right now, no lag. Confirmed live, public, reachable with our normal, non-premium keys for any companyId.
post.summary: Get a company's full employee roster + hourly totals

post.description: Just the `hourly` block from employee.getCompanyRoster, without the employee list — the cheapest call for a company's current real employee profit: hourly profit = production * gameStat.getPpMoneyValue - wageCost - managerCost, in money, live right now (`production` is raw production POINTS per hour, the two costs are already money; no lag, unlike work.getStatsByCompany's daily-aggregated and currently ~1-day-delayed figures). `cap` is the company's current max employee slots. Confirmed live, public, reachable with our normal, non-premium keys for any companyId.
post.summary: Get a company's hourly employee production/wage estimate
